items.note: Applications go through the NTTM GREAT portal with a partner incubator. The last instalment is paid as a reimbursement, so plan for working capital. An aggregator reports a July 2026 office memorandum extending the window to 31 Dec 2027; this is not confirmed on an official page, so check the portal for the current window before applying.

items.title: DRDO Technology Development Fund (TDF) for Startups & MSMEs
items.org: Ministry of Defence – DRDO (TDF Directorate)
items.amount: Grant up to 90% of project cost (startup projects typically up to ₹10 crore)
items.summary: DRDO's Technology Development Fund pays milestone-based grant-in-aid to Indian startups and MSMEs that build defence and dual-use technologies listed by the armed forces, covering up to 90% of project cost. Firms register on the TDF portal and then bid against specific technology RFPs as they are published.
eligibility: Indian startup or MSME: public or private limited company, partnership, LLP, OPC or registered sole proprietorship
Owned and controlled by resident Indian citizens, with no more than 49% foreign investment

Under the startup route: DPIIT-recognised, incorporated no more than 3 years before applying, and incubated at a Central or State government-supported incubator with a defence and aerospace track record
No prior government grant for a similar technology; academic and non-profit research bodies can join only as partners with an industry lead
benefits: Grant of up to 90% of project cost, released against milestones over a typical 2-year development period
Startup projects of up to ₹10 crore estimated cost, with up to 20% support available to the host incubator
Guidance from DRDO labs and a route to defence procurement
items.note: This is not one open call. You register on tdf.drdo.gov.in, verify your profile and then apply against technology-specific RFPs as they are posted, each with its own deadline. Check the portal's project list for live RFPs. The official scheme summary also mentions a higher overall project cap of ₹50 crore for some project types.

items.title: Microsoft for Startups (Founders Hub) – Azure Credits
items.org: Microsoft
items.summary: Microsoft's always-open startup programme gives software companies Azure credits that unlock in stages as they show real usage and progress, with the largest tier reserved for startups backed by a Microsoft Investor Network partner. Approved members also get go-to-market help, Marketplace/co-sell routes and, for some, a named Microsoft contact.
eligibility: Privately held, for-profit company building a software product or service it owns
Headquartered in a country where Azure is offered (India qualifies if it appears during Azure sign-up)
Has not raised Series C or later and has received under $350,000 in lifetime free Azure credits
Educational institutions, government bodies, consultancies/agencies and crypto-mining businesses are excluded
benefits: Azure credits of up to $150K, released progressively as usage and milestones are verified
Higher-value benefits earlier for startups with an Investor Network referral code
Go-to-market support, Microsoft Marketplace and co-sell opportunities, startup-specific Azure resources
items.note: Rolling; apply at startups.microsoft.com via 'Get started'. Needs a Microsoft account, legal company name matching incorporation papers, address and payment details, and personal LinkedIn verification. Decisions usually within about three business days. Without an investor referral code you start on a lower credit tier.

items.title: Mastercard Start Path
items.org: Mastercard
items.summary: Mastercard's roughly six-month virtual engagement programme connects funded, revenue-generating startups with Mastercard product teams, partners and customers to pilot and co-build commercial deals. Mastercard may take an option to invest in some participants, but investment is neither the aim nor guaranteed.
eligibility: Has raised outside investment (seed, Series A or later)
Product already live in market and generating revenue, with reference customers
Solution fits Mastercard's strategy, e.g. payments, digital assets, cybersecurity, sustainability or emerging tech
Open to startups from all regions, including India
benefits: Access to Mastercard's global network of issuers, merchants, partners and customers
Mentorship, co-innovation and dedicated pipeline/commercial support
Visibility and credibility from the Mastercard association, plus possible investment
items.note: Applications are taken online with no published window. Shortlisted startups are asked to share more with relevant product teams before selection. No fee is mentioned. Not for idea-stage teams: you need funding, revenue and a live product.

items.title: Cloudflare for Startups
items.org: Cloudflare
items.summary: Cloudflare gives tech startups one year of credits for its developer platform, network and security products, from $10K for bootstrapped teams up to $350K for well-funded startups backed by an affiliated investor. Higher tiers add an account manager and solutions-architect office hours.
eligibility: Incorporated within the last 10 years, for-profit, actively building a technology product
Funded up to Series B, with funding raised in the last 12 months
Live public website and a public presence on LinkedIn, X or GitHub; business email matching the company domain
First-time applicants only; the $100K and $350K tiers need backing from an affiliated partner investor
benefits: Tier 3: $10K credits for bootstrapped/self-funded startups with under $1M raised
Tier 2: $100K and Tier 1: $350K for partner-backed startups, with an account manager and bi-weekly architect office hours at the top tier
items.note: Apply through the 'Apply here' link on the programme page. Review usually takes up to 48 hours, with approval by email. Credits expire after 12 months or when used up. The page does not list eligible countries, so confirm India-based billing works during sign-up.

items.title: Emergent Ventures India
items.org: Mercatus Center (George Mason University)
items.summary: A low-overhead grant and fellowship programme backing ambitious 'zero to one' ideas, with a dedicated India tranche that announced its 20th India cohort in October 2026. It funds individuals and early projects in any field, including first steps toward a company.
eligibility: Open to individuals worldwide aged 13+; choose India under 'My Project Will Affect' to enter the India tranche
One application per applicant and project
Application must be written by the applicant: AI-written applications are screened out (proofreading only)
Best suited to bold, scalable ideas from talented individuals rather than mature businesses
benefits: Grant or fellowship money sized to the project, decided by a small team with little paperwork
Membership of the Emergent Ventures winners' network, with India cohorts publicly announced on Marginal Revolution
items.note: Rolling, with no deadline or batch. Use 'Apply Now' on the Mercatus page and select India in the drop-down. No feedback or status updates are given, and requests for them may go unanswered. Grant sizes are not published.

items.title: Hub71 Access Programme – Cohort 21 (incl. Hub71+ AI)
items.org: Hub71 (Abu Dhabi)
items.summary: Abu Dhabi's tech hub offers selected startups AED 250K of in-kind incentives (housing, office, health insurance, licensing/visas and more) plus AED 250K cash through a SAFE, if they set up a team in Abu Dhabi. Cohort 21 starts in September 2027, and the Hub71+ AI track adds compute and partners such as AWS, NVIDIA, Google for Startups and MBZUAI.
eligibility: Best suited to pre-seed to Series A startups from any country; Indian startups are regularly selected
At least one founder must commit to relocating long-term and building a team in Abu Dhabi
Complete application form plus a PDF pitch deck covering problem, solution, market, traction, funds raised, team and Abu Dhabi plans
For the Hub71+ AI track, AI must be core to the product
benefits: AED 250K flexible in-kind incentives (office, housing, health insurance, licence/visa, growth marketing)
AED 250K cash via SAFE note, plus up to AED 250K more for high performers after one year
Access to Hub71's network of corporate, government and capital partners
items.note: Cohort 21 cut-off is February 2027 (no exact day published). Later applications roll into the next cohort, so intake never closes. Expect a response within about 3 months; pre-deadline applications are reviewed by April 2027. Four-round selection ending with a committee. Cash is equity-linked (SAFE), and relocation is mandatory.

items.title: Thiel Fellowship
items.org: Thiel Foundation
items.summary: A two-year, no-equity grant of $250,000 for young founders and builders who skip or leave university to work full time on a company, research project or other venture. Fellows are based in many countries and don't have to move to San Francisco.
eligibility: Aged 22 or younger
No university degree; current students may apply but must drop out to accept
Individuals worldwide can apply (fellows are based in multiple countries)
Working on an ambitious company, project or invention full time
benefits: $250,000 paid over two years, with no equity taken
Access to the Thiel Fellowship founder network and mentors
items.note: Applications are reviewed year-round through the portal at thielfellowship.my.site.com/apply/s/. Questions go to the fellowship team by email. The catch: you must leave formal education to take the award.

items.title: Colosseum Eternal — Winter 2026–27 Sprint Award
items.org: Colosseum (Solana-focused hackathon organiser and accelerator)
items.summary: An always-on online hackathon where teams anywhere, India included, launch their own four-week build sprint during the November–March window. The strongest product of the round wins a non-dilutive $25,000 award, and standout teams can be considered for Colosseum's accelerator and pre-seed cheque.
eligibility: Open to crypto developers and startup founders worldwide; no country restriction is stated on the official page
To win the Eternal Award, the startup must not have raised venture capital for the product submitted
Any blockchain can be used for the award, but the accelerator/pre-seed track requires building on Solana
One sprint per team per round; the sprint must be started from the Colosseum dashboard by 20 March 2027
benefits: US$25,000 non-dilutive award paid in USDC stablecoin to the top submission of the round
Possible consideration for US$250,000 pre-seed investment and a place in Colosseum's next accelerator cohort
Written response on every submission within 14 days; shortlisted teams get a short interview with the judges
Fully remote, free to enter
items.note: The last day to START a sprint is Sat 20 March 2027; each sprint then runs four weeks, with optional weekly one-minute progress videos and a final submission (product description, team background, GitHub repo, pitch video, technical demo). Winners are picked around May 2027. Submissions are public by default (can be changed). The award itself is equity-free, but the $250K pre-seed route is an investment and is Solana-only. Payout is in crypto (USDC), so check your bank/FEMA and tax position before accepting.

items.title: Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024 – Tri-Seed Funding (₹2 Lakh)
items.org: Directorate of Information Technology, Government of Tripura (Startup Tripura)
items.summary: A one-time ₹2 lakh seed grant that Tripura pays to idea-stage startups once they hold a recognition certificate under the Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024. You claim it on the state startup portal; there's no competition round.
eligibility: Must be a Private Limited Company, LLP or registered partnership firm incorporated within the last 10 years
Annual turnover must not have exceeded ₹25 crore in any previous financial year
Registered address and a fully working office must be in Tripura
At least 50% of salaried skilled staff must be from Tripura
Must hold a 'Recognized Start-Up' certificate issued through the Startup Tripura portal
Entities formed by demerger or restructuring of an existing business, and franchisees, are excluded
benefits: ₹2 lakh one-time grant released after recognition
Can be combined with the policy's monthly operational-cost reimbursement and later prototype, marketing and patent support
State aims to pay claims within 30 days of a complete submission
items.note: Rolling: the policy took effect on 1 April 2024 and stays in force until it is replaced. Get recognition first (the portal says this takes about 45 days): the Executive Committee screens your application and the State Level Start-Up Council approves it. Then claim the grant on the same portal. Benefits stop once turnover exceeds ₹25 crore.

items.title: Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024 – Monthly Operational Cost Reimbursement (₹20,000/month)
items.org: Directorate of Information Technology, Government of Tripura (Startup Tripura)
items.amount: ₹20,000/month for up to 12 months (+10% women-led, +20% PwD-led)
items.summary: Tripura's version of a sustenance allowance: recognised early-stage startups get back up to ₹20,000 a month of running costs, such as rent, electricity and internet, for their first year after recognition. Women-led and disability-led startups get a top-up.
eligibility: Must be a startup recognised under the Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024 (Pvt Ltd, LLP or partnership, under 10 years old, turnover up to ₹25 crore)
Must have a registered and working office in Tripura, with at least half of its skilled staff from the state
Must declare on the portal that it is operating and working on prototype design or development
Women-led startups qualify for 10% extra; startups led by a person with at least 40% disability qualify for 20% extra (certificate needed at recognition)
benefits: Reimbursement of up to ₹20,000 per month toward operating costs such as rent, power and internet
Paid for up to one year, counted from the date of the recognition certificate
10% extra for women-led startups and 20% extra for PwD-led startups
items.note: Rolling; claims are filed on the Startup Tripura portal only. The 12-month clock starts on the recognition date, not the claim date, so apply soon after you are recognised. This is a reimbursement, so keep bills and rent receipts. The policy has been in force since 1 April 2024 with no end date.

items.title: Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024 – Prototype Stage Reimbursement (up to ₹10 Lakh)
items.org: Directorate of Information Technology, Government of Tripura (Startup Tripura)
items.summary: Once the State Level Start-Up Council accepts its proof of concept, a recognised Tripura startup can claim up to ₹10 lakh back on what it spent building the prototype. Most of the claim must go on materials and equipment.
eligibility: Must be recognised under the Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024
The proof of concept must be approved by the State Level Start-Up Council (SLSC)
At least 75% of the claim must be raw materials, components or capital equipment
Manpower costs may make up no more than 25% of the claim
benefits: Need-based reimbursement of up to ₹10 lakh for manpower, raw materials, components and equipment
10% extra for women-led startups and 20% extra for PwD-led startups
Payment targeted within 30 days of a verified claim
items.note: Rolling; claim through the portal after SLSC approves your proof of concept. You spend first and are reimbursed afterwards, so plan cash flow. Respect the 75:25 split between materials/capex and manpower or the claim will be cut.

items.title: Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024 – Marketing & Publicity Assistance (up to ₹5 Lakh)
items.org: Directorate of Information Technology, Government of Tripura (Startup Tripura)
items.summary: Recognised Tripura startups that are bringing a product or service to market can claim up to ₹5 lakh of launch marketing back from the state, with fixed caps on each type of spend.
eligibility: Must be recognised under the Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024
Must be at commercialisation stage and launching a product or service
Spending must fall within the policy's caps for each marketing channel
benefits: Up to ₹5 lakh reimbursement for launch marketing
Digital and social media can be up to 50% of the claim; trade shows and print/TV/radio ads up to 15% each; contests and free samples up to 10% each
GST paid in Tripura can also be reimbursed under the state's TIIPIS 2022 scheme
items.note: Rolling; claim on the Startup Tripura portal with invoices. The caps for each channel apply to the claimed amount, so spending everything on one channel, such as paid social, means you can't claim the full ₹5 lakh. The policy has been in force since 1 April 2024.

items.title: Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024 – Patent Filing Reimbursement (₹2 Lakh India / ₹10 Lakh Foreign)
items.org: Directorate of Information Technology, Government of Tripura (Startup Tripura)
items.amount: Up to ₹2 lakh per Indian patent; up to ₹10 lakh for foreign patents
items.summary: Tripura pays back patent costs for incubated, recognised startups: up to ₹2 lakh for each Indian patent and up to ₹10 lakh for foreign filings on one invention, in two instalments.
eligibility: Must be recognised under the Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024
Must be an incubated startup, as the policy requires
Foreign-patent support is capped for each subject matter (one invention)
benefits: Up to ₹2 lakh for each Indian patent awarded
Up to ₹10 lakh for foreign patents on a single subject matter
Paid 50% after filing and 50% after the patent is granted
items.note: Rolling; claim on the Startup Tripura portal. The second half is paid only once the patent is granted, which can take years. Keep the filing receipts and attorney invoices.

items.title: Startups Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) — Free Facilitators & Fee Rebates
items.org: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Startup India) with the Office of the CGPDTM (IP India)
items.amount: Facilitator fees fully paid by the government + 80% patent-fee and 50% trademark-fee rebate
items.summary: A standing central scheme that lets recognised startups file patents, trademarks and designs through empanelled IP attorneys whose professional fees are borne by the Government of India, while the startup pays only reduced statutory fees. Patent applications from startups can also be put on a faster examination track.
eligibility: Must be a startup recognised under the Startup India (DPIIT) framework
Filing must be for a patent, trademark or industrial design in India
The application has to be routed through one of the facilitators listed on the Startup India / IP India portal to get the fee-free professional help
Only official (statutory) filing fees remain payable by the startup, at the reduced startup rate
benefits: Government covers the facilitator's professional charges for any number of patent, trademark or design filings
Startups pay 80% less than other companies on patent filing fees
50% rebate on trademark filing fees under the amended Trademark Rules
Option of expedited examination so a startup's patent can be granted sooner
items.note: No application window — it is an always-on benefit. Pick a facilitator from the list on the Startup India IPR page and contact them directly; keep your DPIIT recognition certificate handy as proof of startup status. The facilitator's fee is reimbursed to them by the government, so you should not be billed for professional charges — but statutory government fees (and any extra services like prior-art searches the facilitator may quote separately) are still on you.

items.title: BIRAC SEED Fund — Equity up to ₹30 Lakh via BioNEST Incubators (e.g. Venture Center, Pune)
items.org: BIRAC (Department of Biotechnology), implemented through BioNEST incubators such as Venture Center, Pune
items.summary: BIRAC's SEED Fund puts up to ₹30 lakh of equity into post-proof-of-concept biotech and medtech startups through selected BioNEST incubators. Venture Center in Pune runs an always-available application form for its tranche of the fund.
eligibility: Private limited company (or in the process of incorporating) that is at least 51% owned by Indian citizens — OCI/PIO holdings don't count towards this
Incorporated within the last 5 years, with annual turnover never above ₹25 crore
Technology- or IP-led product venture, chiefly in biotech or biomedical areas, past proof of concept
At least one full-time founder, a written business plan and credible potential to raise follow-on funding
Must be (or become) a resident incubatee of the implementing incubator when the money is invested, and meet its EHS norms
benefits: Equity investment of up to ₹30 lakh per startup from a government-backed fund
Board seat/observer support and periodic review by the incubator's SEED Fund committee
Access to the host BioNEST incubator's labs, mentors and investor network
Positions the startup for BIRAC's larger LEAP Fund and AcE Fund-backed rounds
items.note: Rolling — no closing date shown; confirm your fit with the Seed Fund Team (funding@venturecenter.co.in) before applying. Catches: the incubator takes up to 10% equity, places a nominee director/observer on your board, and requires half-yearly presentations plus annual financial reporting. You must be physically incubated at the implementing incubator (Venture Center is in Pune), so non-local founders may need to relocate — other BioNEST incubators run their own SEED Fund tranches with similar terms.

items.title: C-CAMP Wadhwani Innovation Network (WIN) Centre of Excellence — Non-Dilutive Funding
items.org: C-CAMP (Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms), Bengaluru, with the Wadhwani Foundation
items.summary: A standing C-CAMP call that gives Indian life-science startups and academic innovators up to ₹1 crore of non-dilutive money to push a technology past TRL 4 through pilots, validation and scale-up. Proposals are reviewed on a monthly cycle.
eligibility: Indian startups or academic innovators (faculty/researchers) can apply
Technology must already be beyond TRL 4 and be translation-oriented with clear commercial potential
Must be a product or process innovation (not a service) that is novel and has IP potential
Domains: healthcare, drugs, medical devices, diagnostics, industrial biotechnology or agriculture
Team should show both technical and business capability, with a business model, commercialisation roadmap and understanding of end users and market size
benefits: Up to ₹1 crore per selected awardee, described by C-CAMP as non-dilutive
Can be used for pilot and validation studies, prototype refinement and scale-up work
Funds the data and validation evidence needed to raise the next round of funding
Association with C-CAMP's bio-innovation ecosystem in Bengaluru
items.note: Rolling call: proposals should reach C-CAMP before the 20th of each month to be taken up in that month's cycle (next cut-off 20 December 2026). Applications and queries go by email to win_coe@ccamp.res.in. The page does not spell out project duration, document format, IP or royalty terms — ask before applying. Pure services or tech below TRL 4 won't qualify.

items.title: NIDHI-PRAYAS Prototype Grant at MaDeIT (IIITDM Kancheepuram)
items.org: MaDeIT Innovation Foundation, IIITDM Kancheepuram (DST NIDHI-PRAYAS centre)
items.summary: MaDeIT, the incubator at IIITDM Kancheepuram in Chennai, is accepting applications for DST's PRAYAS grant, which pays individual innovators and young startups up to ₹10 lakh to turn an idea into a working physical prototype.
eligibility: Indian citizens aged 18 or above with government-approved proof of nationality, or Indian startups
Startups must be no older than 7 years from incorporation, with annual turnover never above ₹25 lakh in any financial year
Applicant must own the know-how and IP; employees or students of academic/R&D institutions need an NOC
Must register for pre-incubation or incubation at the MaDeIT TBI for the whole project period after selection
PRAYAS support can be taken only once for the same concept
benefits: Grant of up to ₹10 lakh per innovator/incubatee to build a prototype
IP created under the project stays with the innovator or startup
Incubation support at MaDeIT, IIITDM Kancheepuram
Preference for women, young innovators, bootstrapped teams and projects with a clear path to market
items.note: The official page states the call is open now but gives no closing date, so treat it as rolling and apply early. Apply through the Google Form on the page; a programme brochure and business-plan template are provided there. Grantees must remain incubated at MaDeIT (Chennai) for the project duration — check whether physical presence is required.

items.title: Mookerji Innovation Fund (MIF) for BITSian Founders
items.org: PIEDS, BITS Pilani (endowed by alumnus Sid Mookerji / Silicon Road Ventures)
items.summary: An alumni-endowed fund at BITS Pilani's incubator that writes equity cheques of ₹5–50 lakh into startups founded by current BITS students or recent graduates, with a mentorship track and a possible route to follow-on money from Silicon Road Ventures.
eligibility: At least one founder must be a BITSian
Open to current students of the Pilani, Goa, Hyderabad and Dubai campuses, and alumni who graduated within the last 5 years
Idea-stage teams can apply; incorporation is not needed to apply but may be required before investment
Sector-agnostic, with stated interest in deep tech, women-led, student-led and high-risk moonshot ideas
benefits: Equity investment of ₹5 lakh to ₹50 lakh per startup
3-month mentorship programme with global mentors and bootcamps (Campus Engagement Track)
Coaching from Silicon Road Ventures, PIEDS and partner teams, plus a playbook of operating routines
Selected startups may get follow-on funding from Silicon Road Ventures and a bridge to the US market
items.note: No deadline is published — the page shows a standing Apply Now form, so applications appear to be accepted on a rolling basis. Investment is made against equity; stake and valuation terms are not disclosed. Only for BITS students and alumni of the last five years. Queries: mi.fund@pieds-bitspilani.org.

items.title: NIDHI Seed Support at Venture Center, Pune
items.org: Venture Center (Entrepreneurship Development Center), Pune — DST NIDHI-SSS host incubator
items.summary: Venture Center, the CSIR-NCL-linked science incubator in Pune, invests up to ₹1 crore of DST NIDHI seed money in technology startups to carry them from idea to the point where they can raise angel/VC money or bank loans.
eligibility: Must be a registered Indian startup incorporated as a private limited company
Indian promoters must hold at least 51% (OCI/PIO count as Indian); subsidiaries of MNCs or foreign firms are excluded
Needs at least one dedicated full-time entrepreneur, a formal business plan and a technically sound idea with a strong technology/knowledge component
Must be, or agree to become, a resident incubatee of Venture Center and complete three months of residency before the investment is made
Founders must be willing to give equity in return
benefits: Seed investment of up to ₹1 crore (request must be below ₹100 lakh)
Residency and incubation support at Venture Center's labs and facilities in Pune
Board-level guidance through a Venture Center nominee director/observer
Positioning for follow-on angel, VC or debt funding
items.note: Standing seed fund with an application form on the official page; no deadline or cohort window is published. This is equity, not a grant: Venture Center takes a stake and a board nominee/observer seat, and expects bi-annual presentations to its seed fund committee plus annual financials. Requires physical residency in Pune for at least 3 months before investment. Contact: funding@venturecenter.co.in, +91-9156465104.

items.title: Build with Gemini – Shape What's Next (Voice AI Hackathon 2026)
items.org: YourStory with Google Cloud India and Hack2skill
items.summary: A national voice-AI hackathon run by YourStory on Google Cloud, where builders pitch and then prototype voice-first products using Gemini. Eight teams share an ₹8 lakh cash pool, and shortlisted teams also get Google Cloud credits.
eligibility: Open to working professionals such as developers, AI/ML engineers, data scientists and technical founders
Enter alone or as a team of up to four people
Students and non-professionals cannot enter this edition
Register and submit an idea before the deadline to be considered for shortlisting
benefits: Winner receives ₹3 lakh; first runner-up ₹2 lakh; second runner-up ₹1.25 lakh
Five consolation awards of ₹35,000 each
US$100 in Google Cloud credits for each shortlisted team
Visibility through YourStory's coverage of the hackathon
items.note: Registration and idea submission close on 3 December 2026; the announcement gives no closing time, so submit by the end of 2 December IST to be safe. Registration runs through Hack2skill (the announcement does not print the direct link). It is a prize for individuals or teams, not company funding, and student teams are excluded.

items.title: XPRIZE Accelerate Learning — Core Track (India region)
items.org: XPRIZE Foundation, supported in India by the British Asian Trust
items.summary: A multi-year global prize that rewards teams able to prove, through independent randomised trials, that their approach lifts foundational literacy and numeracy among first-grade children at very low cost. India is one of only two competition regions, making this a rare large-purse prize aimed squarely at Indian classrooms.
eligibility: Open to startups, nonprofits, universities, student teams and independent innovators from any discipline; individuals can join or form a team
Each team picks one region per track at registration — India or Sub-Saharan Africa
Solutions must target at least a 25% improvement in mastery across roughly 150,000 Grade 1 learners at under US$10 per child per year
Impact must be validated through an independent randomised controlled trial run as part of the competition
benefits: Share of a US$5 million Core Track purse, with winners named in 2029
Staged recognition: qualified teams announced in 2027 and finalists in 2028
Global visibility through XPRIZE and access to its partner and funder network
Rigorous third-party evidence of learning impact that can support later fundraising and government partnerships
items.note: Core Track registration closes 15 March 2027 (XPRIZE marks these dates as preliminary and has not published a cut-off time, so register well ahead). A registration fee applies per track but the amount is not shown on the public page; check the team portal before committing. This is a long competition (2026–2029) requiring sustained field implementation and trial participation, not a quick pitch contest.

items.title: XPRIZE Accelerate Learning — Last Mile Moonshot Track
items.org: XPRIZE Foundation with ShikshaNext
items.summary: The ambitious sister track of XPRIZE Accelerate Learning, seeking teacher-co-designed technology that doubles down on hard-to-reach learners with a 50% jump in foundational learning mastery. Indian edtech teams can register for the India region.
eligibility: Open to startups, nonprofits, academic groups, student teams and individual innovators (as part of a team)
Teams choose India or Sub-Saharan Africa as their region at registration
Solutions must aim for at least a 50% gain in mastery at under US$40 per child per year
Technology must be developed together with teachers, and results must hold up in an independent randomised trial
benefits: Share of a US$1 million prize purse
Qualified teams and semi-finalists announced in 2027, finalists in 2028, winners in 2029
Exposure to XPRIZE, ShikshaNext and education funders working on foundational learning
Independent impact evidence usable with state education departments and investors
items.note: Registration for this track closes 15 February 2027 — a month earlier than the Core Track; XPRIZE lists the dates as preliminary and gives no time of day. A per-track registration fee applies (amount not published on the main page). Teams may enter both tracks but must register separately.

items.title: Mozilla Foundation Fellowship 2027–28
items.org: Mozilla Foundation
items.summary: A 12-month paid fellowship for technologists, builders and advocates working on a more trustworthy, open technology future. Independent fellows receive a large personal stipend plus a project budget to pursue their own idea, which suits founders building public-interest or open-source tech.
eligibility: Anyone can apply directly — the call is open internationally, with no nomination needed
Work must align with one of Mozilla's published focus areas, or be submitted as a 'Wildcard' idea
Track I fellows are embedded with a host civil-society organisation; Track II fellows pursue their own independent project
Applicants must be available for a 12-month fellowship starting 1 June 2027
benefits: Track II (Independent): US$100,000 stipend plus US$25,000 project budget (US$125,000 total)
Track I (Embedded): US$75,000 stipend plus US$25,000 project budget (US$100,000 total)
One Independent slot reserved for creative advocacy work
Access to Mozilla's global fellows community and visibility for the project
items.note: Two-stage process: the Letter of Intent is due 17 December 2026 at 11:59 PM Pacific (UTC-8), i.e. about 1:29 PM IST on 18 December. Only a small shortlist is invited to submit a full application, due 12 March 2027 at 11:59 PM Pacific. This is a fellowship for an individual's work, not company investment — read the full RFP and FAQ for any restrictions on running a for-profit venture alongside it.

items.title: KSUM Soft Loan Scheme for Women Entrepreneurs
items.org: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
items.amount: Up to ₹15 lakh at 6% simple interest
items.summary: A purchase-order-backed working-capital loan from KSUM for women-led Kerala startups that have won work from Kerala government departments or PSUs. It funds up to 80% of the order value at a concessional 6% simple interest.
eligibility: Women-led startup registered in Kerala as a Private Limited company or LLP, holding an active KSUM Unique ID
DPIIT recognition and an 'Active' MCA status (Form INC-22A must be filed before money is released)
Must be building an innovative product or technology; pure service firms and trading SMEs are generally excluded
Must hold a confirmed purchase/work order from a Kerala government department or public sector undertaking
No outstanding dues to KSUM, state incubators or any government agency, and not blacklisted; a director CIBIL score above 750 is preferred
benefits: Working capital of up to 80% of the government purchase order, with a maximum outstanding of ₹15 lakh
Concessional 6% simple interest
Released in step with client-certified project milestones
No equity dilution
items.note: Rolling: KSUM's funding page lists this loan with an active 'Apply Now' button (Zoho form) and no closing date. Repayment falls due within one year or on project completion, whichever is earlier. Only orders from Kerala government bodies/PSUs qualify. Scheme manager contact is listed on the page (shahil@startupmission.in).

items.title: KSUM Scaleup Seed Fund (Soft Loan up to ₹25 Lakh)
items.org: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
items.amount: Up to ₹25 lakh soft loan at 6%
items.summary: A collateral-free growth loan from Kerala Startup Mission for product startups that already have meaningful revenue or angel/VC backing. It carries 6% simple interest with a one-year moratorium and three-year repayment.
eligibility: Private Limited company registered in Kerala with active MCA status, DPIIT recognition and a KSUM Unique ID
Building and commercialising an indigenous product or technology; service and trading businesses generally do not qualify
At least ₹25 lakh revenue from the product in the last four quarters, OR at least ₹25 lakh raised from an angel network or VC
At least ₹5 lakh revenue in the quarter before applying (month-on-month growth is preferred)
No pending government dues and not blacklisted by any Indian government agency
benefits: Up to ₹25 lakh per startup (the page's headline badge shows ₹15 lakh, while the overview and FAQ state ₹25 lakh)
6% simple interest, 12-month moratorium, then 36 monthly instalments; prepayment without penalty
Can be used for product enhancement, expansion, marketing and licences/certifications
Startups already holding a KSUM seed loan may be considered for a higher limit
items.note: Rolling: shown with 'Apply Now' on KSUM's Early Stage Funding page, no close date. Two-part online application (Business Profile + Seed Proposal); incomplete forms are rejected. Selection runs through a KSUM call, then a final pitch to the Seed Expert Committee; funds are released in instalments. Some funding may be structured as convertible instruments (CCD/CCPS), so check the guidelines.

items.title: KSUM International & National Exposure Programme (Event Reimbursement)
items.org: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
items.amount: Up to ₹2 lakh per event; ₹5 lakh over 3 years
items.summary: KSUM reimburses Kerala startups for showcasing at national and international trade shows and startup events, covering stall, registration, travel and exhibition costs. Each request is approved event by event.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup with a valid KSUM Unique ID
Must have a Minimum Viable Product; scale-up stage startups get priority
Up to two event trips per financial year
Event choice must be justified by business, investment or market opportunity
benefits: Up to ₹2 lakh reimbursed per event (stall, registration, travel, exhibition space)
Up to ₹5 lakh in total across three years from the first approved event
Support may be raised for strong products, high revenue growth or major events
Decision from KSUM within 7 days of the request
items.note: Rolling, apply per event: email the event details, budget, attendees and expected outcomes to the KSUM address given on the scheme page BEFORE attending. Capped at 50 startups and ₹1.5 crore per year, so budget can run out. A rejected request can be appealed within 2 working days.

items.title: Tamil Nadu SC/ST Startup Fund
items.org: StartupTN (Tamil Nadu Startup and Innovation Mission), MSME Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
items.amount: Equity/debt investment (≈₹1.4 Cr average so far)
items.summary: A state-run fund that invests equity (or debt) in startups controlled by Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe founders from Tamil Nadu. By end-2025-26 it had backed 43 startups with about ₹60.8 crore.
eligibility: SC/ST founders must together hold more than 50% of the equity and control the company
Company domiciled in Tamil Nadu with its main operations in the state
Applying SC/ST founders must be natives of Tamil Nadu or of Tamil origin
Scalable business models and ventures based on indigenous traditional knowledge are encouraged
benefits: Direct equity (or debt) investment from the Government of Tamil Nadu; portfolio investments have averaged roughly ₹1.4 crore per startup
Mentorship, market-access and investor-connect programmes for portfolio startups
Government shareholding has helped portfolio companies raise ₹21.66 crore in follow-on funding
items.note: Rolling under the Tamil Nadu Startup & Innovation Policy 2023 (valid five years). Applications are processed in batches, first-in first-out, and intake may pause once a threshold is reached; evaluation can take 4–6 months and includes business, legal and financial due diligence. The state becomes a shareholder. Apply via the StartupTN portal (registration required).

items.title: StartupTN Patent & Trademark (IPR) Cost Reimbursement
items.org: StartupTN, Government of Tamil Nadu
items.amount: 75% of patent costs, up to ₹3 lakh per patent
items.summary: Under the Tamil Nadu Startup and Innovation Policy 2023, startups can recover a large share of what they spend registering patents, trademarks and geographical indications. Patents get 75% back up to ₹3 lakh each.
eligibility: Startup registered with StartupTN and operating in Tamil Nadu
DPIIT-recognised startup as defined by the Government of India
Claim relates to intellectual property (patent, trademark or GI) registered by the startup
Expenses must be actually incurred and documented
benefits: 75% of patent registration costs, capped at ₹3 lakh per registration
50% of trademark and geographical-indication costs, capped at ₹25,000
Non-dilutive reimbursement
items.note: Rolling reimbursement claimed through the StartupTN portal after costs are incurred; the policy is valid five years from 2023 notification or until replaced. The policy annex is internally inconsistent on the patent figure (it also cites ₹1 lakh), so confirm the current cap with StartupTN before filing.

items.title: Gramam Thorum Puthozhil (GTP) – Village Startup Seed Grant
items.org: StartupTN (TANSIM) with the MSME Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
items.summary: A Tamil Nadu programme aiming to seed 100 startups in 100 selected villages, giving rural founders a ₹1 lakh equity-free grant plus incubation and mentoring through regional hubs and incubators.
eligibility: Rural founders/startups from the villages covered by the programme in Tamil Nadu
Shortlisting on innovation potential, social relevance and feasibility, following the TANSEED SOP
Selected teams must attend the capacity-building and incubation sessions
Outreach prioritises women, SC/ST communities, persons with disabilities and youth
benefits: ₹1 lakh equity-free seed grant (subject to Evaluation Committee approval)
Incubation help with business model, market validation, legal, branding and pitch readiness
Mentorship and orientation, with CSR partners offering infrastructure, networks and market access
items.note: Applications are taken via an 'Apply Now' Google Form on the official GTP page; no closing date is published, so apply early as intake is limited to about 100 startups. Grant release depends on committee approval under TANSEED criteria.

items.title: AP Innovation & Startup Policy 4.0 – Startup Grant (up to ₹20 Lakh for Women/SC/ST/BC-led)
items.org: Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society (APIS), ITE&C Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
items.amount: Up to ₹15 lakh (₹20 lakh for women/SC/ST/BC/minority-led)
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh's 2024-29 startup policy offers phased, non-repayable grants to AP-registered startups, with a higher ₹20 lakh ceiling for startups led by women, SC/ST, BC, minority or differently-abled founders.
eligibility: Incorporated in Andhra Pradesh as a Private Limited company, registered partnership or LLP
Within 10 years of incorporation and turnover never above ₹100 crore in any year
Working on innovation, new products/processes or a scalable business model; Section 8 companies, trusts, societies, franchisees and group-sponsored entities are excluded
Must have a project proposal approved by APIS and register on the AP Startup One portal
Can take a grant/seed from only one AP government department (limited exceptions)
benefits: Up-front grant of up to ₹2 lakh, rising to a total of ₹15 lakh released in phases
Higher cap of ₹20 lakh for startups led by women, BC, SC/ST, minority or differently-abled founders
Applications decided within 60 days and money usually disbursed within 60 days of approval
items.note: Rolling: the policy runs from its 24 March 2025 notification until amended (operating guidelines G.O.Ms.No.9, 28 April 2025). Apply on the AP Startup One portal's incentive section, directly or through RTIH hubs/registered incubators. Grants are released in phases tied to milestones and are approved by APIS's Monitoring & Evaluation Committee.

items.title: AP Startup Patent Filing Reimbursement (₹2 Lakh India / ₹10 Lakh Foreign)
items.org: Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society (APIS), Government of Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh refunds half of what eligible startups spend on patent filing, up to ₹2 lakh for an Indian patent and ₹10 lakh for a foreign one, under the Innovation & Startup Policy 4.0.
eligibility: Startup incorporated in Andhra Pradesh (Pvt Ltd, partnership or LLP) and registered on the AP Startup One portal
Within 10 years of incorporation with turnover not exceeding ₹100 crore in any year
Patent expenses must be actually incurred and documented
Not a Section 8 company, trust, society, franchisee or group-sponsored entity
benefits: Reimbursement of 50% of patent filing expenses
Cap of ₹2 lakh per Indian patent
Cap of ₹10 lakh per foreign patent
Decision targeted within 60 days of the claim
items.note: Rolling claim under the AP Innovation & Startup Policy 2024-29 (in force since 24 March 2025 until amended). Claims go through the Incentive Application section of the AP Startup One portal and are vetted by APIS; RTIH hubs and registered incubators can help file and verify. Keep invoices and filing receipts.

items.title: AP Startup Event Participation & Accelerator Fee Reimbursement
items.org: Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society (APIS), Government of Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Two market-access incentives in Andhra Pradesh's startup policy: the state repays most of the cost of exhibiting at one trade fair a year, and half the fee for joining up to two accelerator programmes.
eligibility: Startup incorporated in Andhra Pradesh and registered on the AP Startup One portal
Within 10 years of incorporation; turnover never above ₹100 crore
Event support is limited to one event per year
Accelerator support covers a maximum of two programmes
benefits: 75% of registration, travel and lodging for an event or fair, up to ₹3 lakh, once a year
50% of accelerator programme fees, up to ₹2 lakh per programme (max two programmes)
Non-dilutive reimbursement
items.note: Rolling reimbursement under AP Innovation & Startup Policy 4.0 (2024-29); claim via the AP Startup One incentive portal after spending, with bills and proof of participation. Approval rests with APIS's Monitoring & Evaluation Committee (decision within ~60 days). The ₹7 lakh figure assumes one event plus two accelerators.

items.title: Karnataka Startup Patent Subsidy (Startup Policy 2025-30)
items.org: Startup Karnataka / Karnataka Innovation & Technology Society (KITS), Dept. of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka
items.amount: 75% of patent costs, up to ₹15 lakh/year
items.summary: Karnataka-registered startups can claim back most of what they spend on Indian and foreign patents under the state's 2025-30 Startup Policy, for up to five patent applications a year.
eligibility: Registered with KITS / Startup Karnataka and operating in Karnataka
Meets the central startup definition: within 10 years of incorporation (20 for recognised deep tech) and turnover under ₹200 crore (₹300 crore for deep tech)
Patent fees already paid; patents with a change of assignee are excluded
Not already reimbursed for the same patent under another Karnataka or Government of India scheme
Claim filed within one year of the patent filing date
benefits: 75% of actual patent expenses, capped at ₹15 lakh per year (Indian and foreign filings both count; provisional applications excluded)
Up to five patent applications claimed per year
Two routes: part-payment soon after filing, or full claim (including attorney fees) after grant
items.note: Rolling claim via the Startup Karnataka portal; needs bank statements, invoices/receipts, an expenditure statement and a notarised affidavit (Annexure 10.2). Sanction depends on the Approval Committee and available budget. CAUTION: the official incentives page still shows the older ₹2 lakh (India)/₹10 lakh (foreign) caps; the 75%/₹15 lakh terms come from the 2025-30 policy (GO dated 14 Nov 2025) as reported by independent sources. For patents filed before 14 Nov 2025, ask the Startup Cell which policy applies.

items.title: Rajasthan iStart Pre-Seed (Ideation) Grant — ₹2.4 Lakh
items.org: iStart Rajasthan, Department of Information Technology & Communication (DoIT&C), Government of Rajasthan
items.summary: Under the Rajasthan Startup Policy 2022, iStart gives pre-seed startups a one-time grant of ₹2.4 lakh to test and shape an idea, with an extra ₹60,000 when women founders hold the majority of equity.
eligibility: Startup must first be registered on the iStart Rajasthan portal
Must be at pre-seed stage, with the idea cleared by the state's Evaluation Committee
Entity must be registered in Rajasthan or run an operating office in the state (proprietorship, partnership, LLP, OPC or private limited company)
The ₹60,000 top-up applies only where women founders hold more than 50% of the equity
benefits: Non-dilutive grant of ₹2,40,000 per eligible startup
Additional ₹60,000 for majority women-owned startups
Access to the wider iStart pipeline, including QRate rating and the larger viability grants that follow
items.note: Rolling — policy-based support, no published closing date; apply after iStart registration via istart.rajasthan.gov.in/startup-apply. Detailed eligibility is notified by the state from time to time and approval rests with the Evaluation Committee. Policy was notified in 2022, so confirm it is still in force before applying.

items.title: Rajasthan iStart Seed-Stage Viability Grant — up to ₹60 Lakh (QRate-linked)
items.org: iStart Rajasthan, Department of Information Technology & Communication (DoIT&C), Government of Rajasthan
items.summary: Seed-stage Rajasthan startups can receive a viability grant whose size is tied to their iStart QRate score — ₹10 lakh for non-rated registered startups, rising through ₹20/30/40 lakh in the Bronze bands to ₹60 lakh for Silver and above.
eligibility: Must be registered under iStart Rajasthan
Seed-stage startup registered in, or operating from, Rajasthan
Grant slab depends on QRate category (non-rated, Bronze 1–20, 20–40, 40–50, or Silver and above); non-rated startups are subject to committee evaluation
Must meet any further criteria the state notifies from time to time
benefits: ₹10 lakh (non-rated) to ₹60 lakh (Silver and above) non-dilutive grant
Upgrade bonus: improving your QRate score within the window (3 months for Bronze, 18 months for Silver+) unlocks the difference for the higher slab
Part of the single-window iStart platform covering incubation and further funding
items.note: Rolling — no fixed deadline; register on iStart, obtain a QRate assessment, then apply via istart.rajasthan.gov.in/startup-apply. Upgrade windows are counted from the date of the latest QRate upgrade. Confirm the 2022 policy remains in force before applying.

items.title: Rajasthan iStart Scale-Up Fund — up to ₹2 Crore (Debt Convertible to Grant)
items.org: iStart Rajasthan, Department of Information Technology & Communication (DoIT&C), Government of Rajasthan
items.amount: Up to ₹2 crore (max 50% of funds raised)
items.summary: Growth-stage Rajasthan startups that have raised outside capital can get state support worth up to half of what they raised, given as debt that converts to a grant, capped at ₹1 crore (Bronze), ₹1.5 crore (Silver) or ₹2 crore (Gold and above).
eligibility: Growth-stage startup registered on iStart Rajasthan with a QRate rating
Must have raised external funds — support is limited to 50% of the total raised
Must satisfy the committee's notified qualifying criteria
Cannot be combined with the Startup Equity Fund — growth-stage startups pick one
benefits: Ceiling of ₹1 crore (Bronze), ₹1.5 crore (Silver) or ₹2 crore (Gold and above)
Instrument is debt that converts to grant, so no equity is given up
Upgrade bonus if QRate improves within 18 months (Silver) or 30 months (Gold+), still capped at 50% of funds raised
items.note: Rolling — no closing date published. The conversion-to-grant conditions are set by the state and are not detailed on the portal page, so read the notified guidelines first. Mutually exclusive with the Startup Equity Fund.

items.title: Rajasthan Startup Equity Fund — Matching Investment up to ₹5 Crore
items.org: iStart Rajasthan, Government of Rajasthan (via the State Alternative Investment Fund)
items.summary: Through a state-backed Alternative Investment Fund, Rajasthan matches the capital an eligible growth-stage startup raises, up to ₹5 crore per company, as an alternative to the Scale-Up Fund.
eligibility: Growth-stage startup registered with iStart Rajasthan
Must have raised funds that the state can match
Must opt for this route instead of the Scale-Up Fund (only one is allowed)
Subject to criteria and diligence by the state AIF
benefits: Government co-investment matching funds raised, up to ₹5 crore per startup
Leverages your existing investor round
Linked into iStart's investor and ecosystem network
items.note: Rolling — no deadline published. This is equity via a state AIF, so expect dilution and standard investor terms; the portal does not publish valuation or instrument details. Cannot be combined with the Scale-Up Fund.

items.title: Gujarat Startup Scheme via VentureStudio (Ahmedabad University) — up to ₹30 Lakh + Monthly Allowance
items.org: Industries Commissionerate, Government of Gujarat, through VentureStudio, Ahmedabad University (nodal institute)
items.amount: Up to ₹30 lakh (+₹10 lakh social-impact top-up) + ₹20,000–25,000/month
items.summary: Gujarat's state startup scheme funds innovators recommended by an approved nodal institute; VentureStudio at Ahmedabad University runs an open application route offering up to ₹30 lakh for product development and marketing, plus a one-year living allowance.
eligibility: Individuals or teams based in Gujarat with a novel product, process or service, recommended by a recognised nodal institute
Entity (LLP, partnership or private limited) incorporated within the last 10 years, with turnover below ₹100 crore in every year
Applicant must have spent at least 2 months in the nodal institute's pre-incubation/incubation and stay incubated full time during support
Not eligible: businesses formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing one, or startups already funded for the same purpose under another Gujarat startup scheme (SSIP excepted)
benefits: Grant of up to ₹30 lakh for prototyping, professional services and marketing
Extra up to ₹10 lakh for projects with strong social benefit
Sustenance allowance of ₹20,000/month for a year (₹25,000 with a woman co-founder)
Further state support listed for approved startups: up to ₹1 lakh soft-skill training, up to ₹3 lakh to join an accelerator, and a 1% extra interest subsidy on term loans (capped at 9%)
items.note: Rolling — VentureStudio's page carries an Apply Now form with no closing date. Final sanction rests with the Government of Gujarat committee and fund availability. You must incubate at the nodal institute (other approved nodal institutes, e.g. PDEU IIC, run the same scheme). Queries: vs@ahduni.edu.in.

items.title: ABIF IIT Kharagpur — Agri-Business Incubation Programme
items.org: Agri Business Incubation Foundation (ABIF), IIT Kharagpur
items.summary: IIT Kharagpur's agri-business incubator is accepting applications for a milestone-based, up-to-12-month incubation programme that gives early agri and food ventures mentoring, lab access and help to secure grants.
eligibility: Open to individuals, proprietary concerns, FPOs/OFPOs, partnerships and LLPs
At least 51% Indian ownership; registered entities must be incorporated in India within the last 10 years
Must be willing to incubate at ABIF for the programme period
Startups incubated elsewhere can apply only after that incubation ends
benefits: Up to 12 months of milestone-based incubation
Technical and product-development mentoring, testing and laboratory access
IP support and business mentoring
Guidance on government grants and investment, with funding depending on the scheme and selection
items.note: Rolling — the programme page shows 'Applications open' with no deadline; apply at abif.iitkgp.ac.in/apply/incubation or email office@abif.iitkgp.ac.in. Selection does NOT guarantee a cash award. Fees and equity terms are not published — ask before signing. (ABIF's MeitY SAMRIDH accelerator is currently closed.)

items.title: Digi-SAPNE 3.0 — North East Startup Acceleration Programme
items.org: AIC-SMU Technology Business Incubation Foundation (AIC-SMUTBI), Sikkim Manipal University, with MeitY funding support
items.amount: Grants (official page says up to ₹80 lakh; the previous cohort paid ₹10 lakh per startup)
items.summary: The third cohort of a MeitY-backed acceleration programme run by AIC-SMUTBI for early-stage tech startups from India's eight North Eastern states. Selected startups get grant support plus growth, market-access and investor-connect tracks that end in a demo day.
eligibility: Early-stage startups from the eight North Eastern states (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura)
Tech-enabled, scalable ventures; this edition gives priority to tourism, agritech and AI
Ventures with some early traction are preferred (the previous edition targeted startups whose growth had stalled)
Registration as a Private Limited company is advised
benefits: Grant funding (the 2.0 cohort received ₹10 lakh per startup)
Growth-hack programme to refine strategy
Market-access programme
Mentorship, workshops and networking
Investors' meet and demo day
items.note: Applications open 1 Oct 2026 and close 5 Dec 2026. No closing time is stated, so submit by 23:59 IST on 4 Dec to be safe. Apply through the form on smutbi.accubate.app (linked from the official page); questions go to sapne@smutbi.com. The official page does not list detailed eligibility, required documents or equity terms. The '₹80 lakh' looks like the programme-wide pool: the 2.0 cohort gave 8 startups ₹10 lakh each (₹80 lakh in total), so amountMax is set conservatively at ₹10 lakh.

items.title: Uttarakhand Startup Policy 2023 – Monthly Sustenance Allowance (up to ₹20,000/month)
items.org: Startup Cell, Department of Industries, Government of Uttarakhand (Startup Uttarakhand)
items.summary: Recognised Uttarakhand startups can draw a monthly living allowance of up to ₹15,000 for a year while they build their product. Startups founded by women, SC/ST, differently-abled or transgender founders, or working on rural-impact or disruptive tech, qualify for up to ₹20,000 a month.
eligibility: Private limited company, LLP or registered partnership incorporated in or operating from Uttarakhand
Recognised by the Uttarakhand Startup Council via the state startup portal
Under 10 years from incorporation with turnover below ₹100 crore
Not formed by splitting or reconstructing an existing business
benefits: ₹15,000 per month for up to 12 months (general)
Up to ₹20,000 per month for women, SC/ST, divyang, transgender-led, rural-impact or disruptive-tech startups
items.note: Sign up on the Startup Uttarakhand portal (Startup India login works), obtain the state Certificate of Recognition, then use 'Apply for Incentives' on the dashboard. Approval is by the Startup Council and is one-time. The 2023 policy replaced the 2018 policy (approved Feb 2023); confirm current cut-offs with the Startup Cell (startupcelluk@gmail.com).

items.title: Uttarakhand Startup Policy 2023 – Seed Fund (up to ₹12.5 Lakh)
items.org: Startup Cell, Department of Industries, Government of Uttarakhand (Startup Uttarakhand)
items.amount: Up to ₹10 lakh (₹12.5 lakh for priority groups; +₹2.5 lakh for disruptive tech)
items.summary: One-time seed support of up to ₹10 lakh for state-recognised startups to take a product to market. Women, SC/ST, divyang and rural startups can get up to ₹12.5 lakh, and disruptive-technology ventures an extra ₹2.5 lakh.
eligibility: Recognised startup under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy
Company, LLP or registered partnership registered in or operating from Uttarakhand
Within 10 years of incorporation and below ₹100 crore turnover
Selection by the Startup Council on merit of the innovation
benefits: Seed grant up to ₹10 lakh
Up to ₹12.5 lakh for women, SC/ST, divyang or rural-area founders
Additional ₹2.5 lakh for disruptive-tech startups
items.note: Apply via 'Apply for Incentives' on the Startup Uttarakhand portal after recognition; keep the pitch deck/business plan and incorporation certificate ready. Released on Startup Council approval and typically in tranches. Amounts confirmed in DPIIT's State Startup Ranking 2026 report for Uttarakhand.

items.title: Uttarakhand Startup Patent Reimbursement (₹1 Lakh India / ₹5 Lakh Foreign)
items.org: Startup Cell, Department of Industries, Government of Uttarakhand (Startup Uttarakhand)
items.amount: 100% of cost, up to ₹1 lakh (Indian) / ₹5 lakh (international) per patent
items.summary: Uttarakhand reimburses the full cost of patenting for recognised startups, capped at ₹1 lakh for an Indian patent and ₹5 lakh for an international one. Payment is split between filing and prosecution stages.
eligibility: Startup recognised under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy
Entity registered in or operating from Uttarakhand
Patent filed in the startup's name
Not already reimbursed under another government scheme
benefits: Up to ₹1 lakh per Indian patent
Up to ₹5 lakh per international patent
Historically 75% released on filing and 25% on prosecution
items.note: Claim through 'Apply for Incentives' on the state startup portal with filing receipts and attorney invoices. Recognition by the Startup Council is required first. Tranche split is from the earlier policy; confirm current procedure with the Startup Cell.

items.title: J&K Startup Policy 2024–27 – Seed Funding up to ₹20 Lakh
items.org: Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute (JKEDI), Department of Industries & Commerce, Govt of J&K
items.amount: Up to ₹20 lakh in four instalments
items.summary: Startups recognised under the J&K Startup Policy 2024–27 can receive one-time seed funding of up to ₹20 lakh, released in four equal tranches, for prototyping, product launch, market entry or scaling. Roughly 25 startups are supported each year.
eligibility: Startup recognised by JKEDI under the J&K Startup Policy 2024–27
Operating in the UT of Jammu & Kashmir
Proposal for a prototype, new product/service, market entry or expansion
Shortlisted by the JKEDI Screening Committee and approved by the Startup Task Force
benefits: Seed grant up to ₹20 lakh
Paid in four equal instalments tied to progress
Pitch feedback from the screening committee
items.note: Register on the J&K startup portal and obtain JKEDI recognition, then apply when JKEDI invites seed-fund proposals (screening rounds held division-wise, e.g. Kashmir and Jammu in Sept–Oct 2025). Two-tier approval: Screening Committee then Startup Task Force. Policy period runs to 2027 and the annual slots are budget-limited.

items.title: Haryana Startup Patent Cost Reimbursement (up to ₹10 Lakh per Foreign Patent)
items.org: Department of Industries & Commerce, Government of Haryana (Startup Haryana)
items.amount: 100% of costs; ₹3 lakh (national) / ₹10 lakh (international) per patent; ₹25 lakh cumulative
items.summary: Haryana pays back the full cost of granted patents for registered Category 1 startups, up to ₹3 lakh per Indian and ₹10 lakh per international patent, with a lifetime ceiling of ₹25 lakh. Filing, search, attorney, maintenance and renewal fees are covered.
eligibility: Category 1 startup: DPIIT-recognised, registered office in Haryana, registered with Startup Haryana
Holds a Haryana Udyam Memorandum (HUM)
Patent granted between 7 July 2022 and 6 July 2027 (Indian patents via a registered agent)
No similar reimbursement claimed under another state or central scheme
benefits: Up to ₹3 lakh per national patent
Up to ₹10 lakh per international patent (conventional or PCT)
Cumulative cap of ₹25 lakh
items.note: Apply online on the Industries & Commerce portal (Annexure I) within 6 months of the patent grant. Documents: grant certificate, HUM, CA-certified expense statement with invoices, notarised undertaking, authorisation letter, audited accounts, cancelled cheque. Trademarks/copyrights excluded. Scheme ends 6 July 2027.

items.title: Haryana Startup Lease Rental Subsidy (45% for Women-Founded Startups)
items.org: Department of Industries & Commerce, Government of Haryana (Startup Haryana)
items.amount: 30% of rent (45% women-only founders), up to ₹5 lakh for one year
items.summary: Haryana refunds 30% of a year's office rent for startups based in a registered incubator, IT park, approved industrial estate or SEZ in the state, rising to 45% where all founders are women. The refund is capped at ₹5 lakh.
eligibility: Category 1 startup registered with Startup Haryana (DPIIT-recognised, registered office in Haryana)
Holds a Haryana Udyam Memorandum (HUM)
Space in a Startup Haryana-registered incubator, notified IT park, approved industrial estate or SEZ in Haryana
Lease in the startup's or founder's name, rent paid from the startup's bank account
benefits: 30% lease rent reimbursement for general startups
45% for startups with only women founders
Maximum ₹5 lakh, covering one year of rent
items.note: File online within six months after the close of the financial year claimed. Attach lease deed, rent payment proof, photos of the space, CA certificate (Annexure IV), HUM, notarised undertaking and cancelled cheque. Cash or personal-account payments are not reimbursed. Covers rent incurred up to 6 July 2027.

items.title: MP Startup Lease Rental Assistance (₹5,000/month for 3 Years)
items.org: MP Start-up Centre / MSME Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh
items.amount: 50% of rent, up to ₹5,000/month for 3 years
items.summary: Under the MP Startup Policy 2025, startups renting workspace in Madhya Pradesh get half their rent reimbursed, capped at ₹5,000 a month, for three years. Product startups in state-owned or aided industrial areas can claim against lease rent and maintenance charges.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup registered on the MP Startup Portal
Workspace located in Madhya Pradesh
Rent paid for an incubator, co-working, office or industrial-area premises
Reimbursement cannot exceed 50% of the amount actually paid
benefits: 50% rent reimbursement
Up to ₹5,000 per month
Available for up to 36 months
items.note: Register on startup.mp.gov.in and apply with the startup application form plus lease agreement and rent receipts. Claims are approved by the State Level Assistance Committee on MP Start-up Centre recommendation. MP GST registration is generally expected for state incentives.

items.title: MP Startup Event Participation Reimbursement (up to ₹1.5 Lakh International)
items.org: MP Start-up Centre / MPLUN, Government of Madhya Pradesh
items.summary: Madhya Pradesh reimburses three-quarters of the cost of exhibiting at or attending a startup event, up to ₹50,000 for an event in India and ₹1.5 lakh abroad. A startup can use it once per financial year and twice in total.
eligibility: Startup registered on the MP Startup Portal (DPIIT-recognised, operating in MP)
Participation in a national or international startup/industry event
One claim per financial year, maximum two in the startup's lifetime
Approval by the Managing Director, MPLUN
benefits: 75% reimbursement of event costs
Cap of ₹50,000 for domestic events
Cap of ₹1,50,000 for international events
items.note: Apply via the MP Startup Portal using the startup application form; keep registration, travel and stall invoices and proof of participation. Seek approval in advance where possible since sanction rests with MPLUN.

items.title: Chandigarh Startup Policy 2025 – Seed/MVP Grant (up to ₹9 Lakh for Women-Led)
items.org: Startup Cell, Department of Industries, Chandigarh Administration
items.summary: Chandigarh funds up to 20 startups a year with grants of up to ₹7 lakh to build and validate an MVP, paid in three tranches through their parent incubator. Women-led and transgender-led startups get an extra ₹2 lakh.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised private limited company, LLP or registered partnership incorporated in Chandigarh or registered with Chandigarh GST
Registered on the Start-In-Chandigarh portal and linked to a recognised parent incubator
Within 10 years of incorporation and under ₹100 crore turnover
Women-led bonus requires a woman founder serving as Chair, MD or CEO until all tranches are paid
benefits: Grant up to ₹7 lakh in three tranches
Additional ₹2 lakh for women-led or transgender-led startups
Disbursed via the parent incubator
items.note: Apply on the Start-In-Chandigarh portal through your parent incubator; applications are reviewed quarterly by the PMIC per the Operational Guidelines notified 1 Jan 2026. Only 20 grants a year, first-come first-served subject to funds. Policy valid five years from April 2025.

items.title: Chandigarh Startup Policy 2025 – Early Growth/Commercialisation Grant (up to ₹14 Lakh)
items.org: Startup Cell, Department of Industries, Chandigarh Administration
items.summary: A second-stage grant of up to ₹12 lakh helps up to 20 Chandigarh startups a year commercialise and scale a validated product, released in three tranches. Women-led and transgender-led startups receive ₹2 lakh more.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup incorporated in Chandigarh or registered with Chandigarh GST
Registered on the Start-In-Chandigarh portal with a recognised parent incubator
Product past MVP and moving to commercialisation
Within 10 years of incorporation and under ₹100 crore turnover
benefits: Grant up to ₹12 lakh in three tranches
Additional ₹2 lakh for women-led or transgender-led startups
Routed through the parent incubator
items.note: Apply via the Start-In-Chandigarh portal through the parent incubator; PMIC evaluates quarterly and fixes deficiencies within 15 days or the file lapses. Capped at 20 startups a year from a ₹4.6 crore combined corpus. Policy runs to about April 2030.

items.title: BIRAC Product Commercialization Program (PCP) Fund — Rolling Call
items.org: BIRAC (Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council), Department of Biotechnology
items.summary: BIRAC co-funds the market launch and scale-up of biotech products that are already validated (TRL 7 or higher), covering things like target-market validation and large-scale commercialisation. Proposals are reviewed in batches through the year, and the current listing gives 31 December 2026 as the closing date.
eligibility: Indian startup incorporated no more than 10 years before the call ends
At least 51% Indian shareholding held by Indian citizens, certified by a CA/CS with UDIN
Nationally relevant product at TRL 7 or above, whether or not BIRAC funded earlier development
Product in a listed focus area such as drugs, vaccines, biosimilars, devices and diagnostics, agri/aqua/veterinary, industrial biotech, bio-based chemicals, smart proteins or synthetic biology
A product that has already received PCP support cannot apply again
benefits: Project support for up to 24 months, released by milestone
Covers market launch, validation in target markets and commercial scale-up
No equity is taken. Support is repaid as a royalty instead
items.note: Apply through the online application form on the BIRAC website. Have your incorporation certificate, a CA/CS shareholding certificate with UDIN and evidence of TRL 7+ and regulatory status ready. Shortlisted applicants present and then go through technical and financial due diligence. Catches: you must fund at least 30% of the project cost yourself, and you repay BIRAC as a royalty within five years of completion (1.5x BIRAC's contribution if the product is commercialised, 1x if not). R&D, product modification and patent costs are not covered.

items.title: AgriSURE Direct Scheme — Equity up to ₹25 Crore for Agri & Rural Startups
items.org: NABVENTURES Ltd (NABARD subsidiary), investment manager of the Agri Fund for Start-ups & Rural Enterprises (AgriSURE)
items.summary: AgriSURE is a ₹750 crore SEBI-registered Category II AIF, backed by the Government of India and NABARD, with a direct scheme that invests equity in agri and rural startups. Proposals are taken on a rolling basis by email, and investments go up to ₹25 crore per company.
eligibility: Startup incorporated in India and recognised by DPIIT
Working in agriculture, allied or rural sectors such as agritech, food processing, animal husbandry, fisheries, supply chain, farm mechanisation or renewable energy
Past the idea and prototype stage, with a steady revenue stream and a differentiated business model
Meeting the criteria does not guarantee investment. NABVENTURES' decision is final
benefits: Direct equity or equity-linked investment (e.g. CCPS) of up to ₹25 crore, subject to AIF rules
Investment released in tranches, with possible follow-on in later rounds
No repayment obligation
items.note: Email your pitch deck or company profile to agrisure@nabard.org (address given on NABARD's AgriSURE FAQ page). There is no application fee, and NABARD warns against agents who ask for money. This is a VC-style investment, so expect equity dilution and full due diligence. Very early (pre-revenue) ventures are better served by AgriSURE-backed sector AIFs or RKVY-RAFTAAR incubators.

items.title: Startup Odisha — Incubation Rent Subsidy (50%, up to ₹5,000/month)
items.org: Startup Odisha, MSME Department, Government of Odisha
items.amount: 50% of rent, up to ₹5,000/month for 1 year
items.summary: Odisha refunds half the monthly rent a recognised startup pays for space at a state-recognised incubator, up to ₹5,000 a month for a year. Startup Odisha lists subsidised incubation among its current startup services, and claims go through its portal.
eligibility: Recognised as a startup by Startup Odisha
Incubated at an incubator recognised by Startup Odisha
Paying monthly rent for incubation space
Support lasts at most one year per startup
benefits: Reimbursement of 50% of the monthly incubation-space rent
Capped at ₹5,000 per month for up to 12 months (about ₹60,000 in total)
items.note: Get Startup Odisha recognition first, then claim through www.startupodisha.gov.in with your incubator agreement and rent receipts. Helpline: 1800 345 7100. The amounts come from the Odisha Startup Policy as amended (2nd Amendment). The official services page lists the benefit but not the amounts, so confirm the current cap on the portal.

items.title: Startup Odisha — Travel & Stall Support for National/International Events
items.org: Startup Odisha, MSME Department, Government of Odisha
items.amount: Economy airfare / 3AC rail fare + free stall
items.summary: Recognised Odisha startups that represent the state at well-known national or international events can have their travel paid (economy air or 3-tier AC rail). When the state government sets up a pavilion, they also get free stall space.
eligibility: Recognised as a startup by Startup Odisha
Representing Odisha at a reputed national or international event, such as a trade fair, expo or summit
Prior approval from Startup Odisha before travelling
Free stall space applies only where the State Government has set up the stall or pavilion
benefits: Economy-class airfare or 3-tier AC train fare to the event
Free stall space in state-organised pavilions
items.note: Apply through www.startupodisha.gov.in before the event, with the event invitation or registration and your travel plan. No fixed rupee cap is published. Support is decided case by case, so get approval before you book. Helpline: 1800 345 7100.

items.title: AIC-NIFIE Incubation with Seed Funding up to ₹5 Lakh
items.org: AIC-NIFIE (Atal Incubation Centre – NITIE Incubation Foundation for Innovation & Entrepreneurship), IIM Mumbai
items.summary: A sector-agnostic Atal Incubation Centre at IIM Mumbai. It takes early tech ventures into physical incubation for 1–2 years, and the strongest can get merit-based seed funding of up to ₹5 lakh.
eligibility: Registered as a private limited company or LLP
Product at proof-of-concept, lab-demo or prototype stage
Has raised no more than ₹1 crore in prior funding
Startups holding patents or copyrights are preferred
benefits: Merit-based seed funding of up to ₹5 lakh
Office space at IIM Mumbai (Powai) for one year, extendable by another year
Business mentoring, networking events, and help finding grants and funding schemes
items.note: Apply through the Google Form linked on the announcement page with your startup details and pitch deck. Shortlisted teams pitch to a selection committee, and selected startups sign an incubation agreement and submit documents. No closing date is published, so it appears to be ongoing. Seed funding is not guaranteed: unfunded startups may be incubated self-financed. Fees and equity terms are not published, so ask aic-nifie@iimmumbai.ac.in.

items.title: SINE IIT Bombay Startup Incubation
items.org: SINE (Society for Innovation & Entrepreneurship), IIT Bombay
items.amount: Up to 3 years' incubation + seed-fund access (amount not stated)
items.summary: IIT Bombay's main business incubator. It takes IP-led, product-focused tech startups into up to three years of physical or virtual incubation and channels them to its seed funds and to government grants.
eligibility: Technology startups built on a product or IP with a scalable model
Open to founders from outside IIT Bombay, including recent graduates and academic spin-offs
Must clear an internal pitch and then a pitch to external domain experts
benefits: Up to 3 years of physical or virtual incubation
Access to SINE-managed seed funds and help applying for government grants
Mentors, IIT Bombay labs and SINE's investor network
items.note: Fill in the online application, then go through the two-stage pitch (SINE team, then external experts). Equity, fee and seed-amount terms are in SINE's 'Policy & Procedure for Incubation' document, not on the main page. Contact sine@sineiitb.org.

items.title: a16z speedrun — Next Residency (rolling applications)
items.org: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)
items.summary: a16z's 12-week in-person accelerator in San Francisco. It invests $500K for 10% upfront through a SAFE and can add up to $500K more in the next round. Applications are reviewed year-round.
eligibility: Very early-stage founders building a new startup
Founders must attend the 12-week residency in San Francisco in person
Applications arriving after a cohort's cut-off roll into the next residency
benefits: $500K on a SAFE for 10%, plus up to $500K more in the next round within 18 months
$10M+ in cloud, AI and software credits from 200+ partners
Founder retreat, Demo Day and a16z network; no board seat
items.note: The SR008 window (residency 1 Feb – mid-Apr 2027) closed on 1 Nov 2026. The apply page says applications are reviewed year-round, and later ones count toward the following residency, whose dates aren't announced yet. Indian founders need to relocate to San Francisco for 12 weeks and sort out a US visa. The 10% equity is substantial for a pre-seed cheque.

items.title: Zoho for Startups — Up to ₹3 Lakh in Zoho Credits
items.org: Zoho Corporation
items.amount: Up to ₹3 lakh in software credits
items.summary: Zoho gives eligible Indian startups up to ₹3 lakh in wallet credits for its 55+ business apps (CRM, Books, Zoho One, etc.). Credits come in a 360-day first stage and a conditional 90-day top-up.
eligibility: Must count as a startup under Startup India guidelines
Must have DPIIT recognition or a link to a Zoho-listed incubator, accelerator or co-working enabler
New or free Zoho user with no paid subscription history
Has not received Zoho for Startups credits before
benefits: Stage 1: about ₹2 lakh in Zoho wallet credits valid for 360 days (usable on bundles such as Zoho One, CRM Plus)
