Stage 2: about ₹1 lakh more in promotional credits for 90 days, depending on first-year usage
Access to 55+ Zoho products
items.note: Create a Zoho account first, using your primary admin email. Then fill in the four-part form with your DPIIT number or chosen enabler, vertical and location, and reply to the eligibility email that arrives about 10 minutes later. The page also shows an older 'up to ₹1.86 lakh' figure, so the final amount may vary. Credits only cover Zoho products, and some stage-2 credits exclude Mail/Workplace.

items.title: MongoDB for Startups — Up to $15,000 Atlas Credits
items.org: MongoDB
items.amount: Up to $15,000 (~₹13 lakh) in Atlas credits
items.summary: MongoDB's rolling startup programme gives up to $15,000 in Atlas database credits plus Voyage AI embedding tokens and technical advice. The credit size depends on stage and on whether a partner VC or accelerator refers you.
eligibility: Company is 7 years old or younger
Raised Series B or less (bootstrapped startups can apply)
Builds a single software product; agencies and dev shops are excluded
Has an active website and LinkedIn page
benefits: Up to $15,000 in MongoDB Atlas credits (12-month validity for credits above $500)
Voyage AI tokens for embedding and reranking models
Free Atlas developer support for 30 days, one-to-one technical advice, co-marketing
items.note: Apply with the online form using your company email, URL, LinkedIn, HQ country and funding stage. A decision usually arrives within five business days. Redeem the promo code under Billing > Apply Code within 30 days or it expires. Bootstrapped startups get baseline credits, and the full $15K usually needs a partner referral.

items.title: ElevenLabs Startup Grants — 12 Months Free Voice AI
items.org: ElevenLabs
items.summary: ElevenLabs gives early startups building with voice AI a year of free platform access and 33 million characters, which it says covers more than 680 hours of voice-agent usage.
eligibility: Early-stage startup building a product that uses ElevenLabs voice or agent technology
Must describe the startup, team and expected growth in the application
Grant is applied to the account used to apply
benefits: 12 months of free access to the full ElevenLabs platform
33,000,000 characters (~680+ hours of Agents usage), valued above $5,500
Founder community events and startup support
items.note: Apply with the short online grant form, and expect a decision within about a week. The page doesn't publish detailed eligibility caps such as funding or team size. The grant covers usage credits only, with no cash.

items.title: FITT IIT Delhi Incubation — Grant Support from ₹4 Lakh to ₹1 Crore
items.org: FITT (Foundation for Innovation and Technology Transfer), IIT Delhi
items.summary: FITT, the technology-transfer and incubation arm of IIT Delhi, gives grants of ₹4 lakh to ₹1 crore to early-stage startups it incubates, for refining an idea, building a prototype or testing the market. You reach the grant by applying for incubation through FITT's standing application, and FITT says it will look at startups from the idea stage onward.
eligibility: Early-stage startups refining a business idea, building a prototype or validating market potential
Must be admitted to FITT incubation; the grant is not a standalone open call
Must submit a fund-utilisation plan tied to clear goals
Funds must be spent according to FITT's guidelines
benefits: Grant of ₹4 lakh up to ₹1 crore, depending on need and the funds available
Incubation and scale-up support, including access to IIT Delhi labs and infrastructure
Help raising capital from seed rounds onward through FITT's network
items.note: Rolling: FITT's funding page sends applicants to its 'Apply for Incubation' form and gives no closing date. FITT says the grant range may change with fund availability, and the amount depends on your utilisation plan. Grants are usually drawn from schemes FITT runs (e.g. TIDE 2.0, BIRAC BIG), so the terms of the matching scheme apply. Incubation fees are not stated, so ask FITT.

items.title: FITT IIT Delhi First-Cheque Investment — Debt or Equity, ₹10 Lakh to ₹1.5 Crore
items.org: FITT (Foundation for Innovation and Technology Transfer), IIT Delhi
items.summary: FITT at IIT Delhi writes first-cheque debt or equity investments of ₹10 lakh to ₹1.5 crore in deep-tech startups that have reached the point where its network can help them scale. Most companies it has funded were somewhere between prototype and post-revenue when they got the money.
eligibility: Startups building deep-tech or breakthrough technology
Usually past the prototype stage: pre-launch, launched or already earning revenue
Must apply through FITT's incubation process
benefits: First-cheque investment of ₹10 lakh to ₹1.5 crore, as debt or equity
Access to IIT Delhi labs, facilities and FITT's investor and industry network
Help with follow-on fundraising
items.note: Rolling: you apply through FITT's 'Apply for Incubation' form, and no closing date is published. FITT's page does not say which deals are debt and which are equity, or what valuation or interest terms apply, so expect to give up equity or take on repayment depending on the deal. Confirm the terms with FITT before applying.

items.title: SIIC IIT Kanpur Seed Fund — Seed Loan of ₹15–25 Lakh for Incubated Startups
items.org: SIIC (Startup Incubation and Innovation Centre), IIT Kanpur
items.summary: SIIC, IIT Kanpur's startup incubator, offers seed loans of ₹15–25 lakh to registered companies it has incubated for at least three months. Each case is decided on the startup's merits under SIIC's Seed Funding Guidelines, and depends on the funds and schemes SIIC has available.
eligibility: Must be a registered company (private limited or similar)
Must have been incubated at SIIC, IIT Kanpur, for at least three months before applying
Approved case by case against SIIC's own criteria and the startup's merits
Depends on the funds, grants or schemes SIIC has at the time
benefits: Seed loan of ₹15 lakh to ₹25 lakh
Incubation at SIIC, IIT Kanpur, including access to the institute's labs and mentors
SIIC can also put incubatees forward for other schemes it handles, such as DSIR PRISM and Ministry of MSME support
items.note: You must already be incubated: this is open only to SIIC incubatees after three months, so apply for incubation first (details on siicincubator.com). IIT Kanpur's page calls it a loan but does not publish the interest, repayment or conversion terms, which are set in SIIC's Seed Funding Guidelines, so ask for those. Rolling, with no closing date.

items.title: TIDE 2.0 Entrepreneur-in-Residence Fellowship at TIDES, IIT Roorkee (₹4 Lakh)
items.org: TIDES Business Incubator, IIT Roorkee (MeitY TIDE 2.0 scheme)
items.summary: TIDES, the business incubator at IIT Roorkee, offers four one-year Entrepreneur-in-Residence fellowships of ₹4 lakh each under MeitY's TIDE 2.0 scheme. The fellowship is for young graduates with no other income who want to spend a year validating and building a technology idea.
eligibility: Indian citizen under 35 years of age
Graduate in science or engineering (BTech, MTech, MSc, PhD, MBBS, MBA or equivalent), or a final-year student who is not taking up a placement
No other source of income during the fellowship
Must not be a promoter, shareholder or beneficiary of another company
Fellowship support stops if you raise outside funding or investment for the idea
benefits: ₹4 lakh fellowship for one year (four fellowships available)
Incubation infrastructure and lab facilities at IIT Roorkee
Mentoring, business support and networking
Preference for women founders, founders under 35 and ideas likely to create manufacturing jobs
items.note: The official page has a live 'Click here to apply' link and no closing date, but it does not say when the next cohort will be chosen, so confirm the current intake at tides_meity@iitr.ac.in. Preferred technologies are AI/ML, blockchain, IoT, cybersecurity and drones. Fellows are expected to work from the TIDES incubator at IIT Roorkee. Equity and fees are not mentioned.

items.title: NIDHI-PRAYAS Prototype Grant at VentureStudio, Ahmedabad University (up to ₹10 Lakh)
items.org: VentureStudio, Ahmedabad University (DST NIDHI-PRAYAS centre)
items.summary: VentureStudio at Ahmedabad University is a DST NIDHI-PRAYAS centre that gives individual innovators and very young startups up to ₹10 lakh to turn a hardware or physical-product idea into a working prototype. The grant pays for outsourced fabrication, raw materials and similar prototyping costs, with capped amounts for travel, patents and contingencies.
eligibility: Indian citizen aged 18 or older; teams must name one lead applicant who applies and receives the funds
Existing PRAYAS incubatees qualify only if the company is under 2 years old, has no significant revenue and is building a new product
Must be a physical product; pure software and pure academic research are not funded
Must register for pre-incubation or incubation at VentureStudio for the whole programme
Applicants who study or work at an institution need a no-objection certificate (NOC); doctoral projects and teaching faculty are not eligible
Support is given only once for the same concept
benefits: Grant of up to ₹10 lakh for building a prototype
Covers outsourcing, raw materials and fabrication, plus capped travel, patent and contingency costs
Pre-incubation or incubation support at Ahmedabad University's VentureStudio
items.note: The official page lets you apply through an online portal or by emailing the form, and gives no closing date. PRAYAS centres often review applications in batches, so check with VentureStudio when the next review is. Priority areas are manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, cleantech, energy, water and IoT. Preference goes to bootstrapped or co-invested projects, women innovators and young innovators. No fees or equity are mentioned.

items.title: TVARAN 3.0 — Maharashtra Tech Accelerator Project (T-MAP)
items.org: Villgro Innovations Foundation (part of Cisco's 40 Communities initiative)
items.amount: Share of a pilot pool of up to ₹3 crore
items.summary: Villgro's third TVARAN cohort funds and supports city pilots of water, wastewater and solid-waste solutions with urban local bodies in Mumbai, Thane and Mira Bhayandar, from a combined pilot pool of up to ₹3 crore.
eligibility: Commercial enterprises with a solution ready to scale in Maharashtra
Solution must be deployable in Mumbai, Thane or Mira Bhayandar
Prior experience working with Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) is expected
Existing ULB partnerships/MoUs, or a credible path to securing one
Focus areas: digital operational intelligence, modular wastewater treatment and reuse, compact solid-waste processing, niche waste streams, waterway and drain protection
benefits: Pilot funding from a cumulative pool of up to ₹3 crore
Validation of the solution in live city environments
Hands-on implementation support to speed adoption by municipal bodies
items.note: Villgro's programmes page lists TVARAN 3.0 under 'Applications open' for 2026 with no closing date published; apply via Villgro's TVARAN portal (vitals.villgroapps.org/tvaran-accelerator). Per-startup grant size, cohort size, equity terms and fees are not stated on the official page — confirm with Villgro before applying.

items.title: DSIR PRISM Phase I — Grants up to ₹20 Lakh for Individual Innovators
items.org: Department of Scientific & Industrial Research (DSIR), Ministry of Science & Technology, via TOCIC host incubators such as Venture Center, Pune
items.amount: Up to ₹2 lakh (Cat. I) or ₹20 lakh (Cat. II), max 90% of project cost
items.summary: DSIR's PRISM scheme gives Indian individual innovators grants to turn an idea into a working prototype: up to ₹2 lakh for proof-of-concept projects costing up to ₹5 lakh, and up to ₹20 lakh for fabrication, testing, patenting and tech transfer on projects of ₹5–35 lakh.
eligibility: Indian citizens with an innovative idea they want to develop into a working prototype, model or process
Individual students, innovators and researchers; also technology providers building solutions for MSME clusters
Category I: project cost up to ₹5 lakh (PoC, prototypes, models)
Category II: project cost ₹5–35 lakh (working models, process know-how, testing/trials, patenting, technology transfer)
Priority areas include green tech, clean energy, smart materials, waste to wealth, affordable healthcare, and water and sewage management
benefits: Category I grant: lesser of ₹2 lakh or 90% of project cost
Category II grant: lesser of ₹20 lakh or 90% of project cost
Non-dilutive government funding
Handholding through DSIR's Technology and Innovation Outreach Centres (TOCICs) such as Venture Center, Pune
items.note: No closing date is published: the government S&T portal lists the scheme, and Venture Center (a DSIR TOCIC) marks it 'Active'. There's no online form on either page, so contact your nearest TOCIC (e.g. frontdesk@venturecenter.co.in, Pune) for the current proposal format and intake schedule. The innovator funds the 10% balance of project cost.

items.title: Atlassian for Startups — 12 Months Free Premium (up to 50 Seats)
items.org: Atlassian
items.amount: 12 months free Jira, Confluence, Loom & Bitbucket Premium (up to 50 seats)
items.summary: Atlassian gives qualifying startups one year of its Premium cloud tools at no cost, covering Jira, Confluence, Loom Business + AI and Bitbucket for up to 50 users, plus smaller seat allowances on its service-management and product-discovery tools.
eligibility: Must not already be a paying Atlassian customer
Must be venture-funded or connected to one of Atlassian's partner accelerators or incubators
Total external funding raised must not exceed US$10 million
Each startup can enrol for only one 12-month period
benefits: Jira Premium, Confluence Premium and Bitbucket Premium for up to 50 seats each
Loom Business + AI for up to 50 seats
Jira Service Management / Customer Service Management for up to 10 seats
Jira Product Discovery Premium with 10 creator seats and unlimited contributors
items.note: Rolling, apply via the request form on the page. Atlassian may ask for proof of funding (e.g. a Crunchbase or PitchBook profile). Marketplace apps are not covered; going above the seat caps means moving to a paid tier, and after 12 months you must renew on paid plans or cancel.

items.title: Notion for Startups — Up to 6 Months Free Business Plan with Notion AI
items.org: Notion Labs
items.amount: Up to 6 months free Business plan + AI (worth up to $12,000)
items.summary: Notion offers early-stage companies free months on its Business plan with Notion AI built in; the length of the free period (1, 3 or 6 months) depends on whether the startup is referred by a Notion partner investor or accelerator.
eligibility: Must not be a paying Notion customer and must not have used an earlier Notion promotion
Fewer than 100 employees
Must sign up with a company-domain work email (no Gmail/Outlook) and have a working business website
6-month tier requires affiliation with a listed Notion partner VC or accelerator; 3-month tier for unaffiliated teams under 100 staff with full business details
benefits: Business plan with Notion AI free for 1, 3 or 6 months depending on tier
Offer valued at up to US$12,000 for a 100-person team
Access to Notion Perks software discounts
One complimentary session with a Notion Certified Consultant (separate application)
items.note: Rolling. Startups without a partner referral or with incomplete details may get only one free month. After the free period the workspace bills at standard Business plan rates unless downgraded.

items.title: PostHog for Startups — $50,000 Product Analytics Credits
items.org: PostHog
items.summary: PostHog, the open-source product analytics and session-replay platform, gives young, lightly funded startups $50,000 in usage credits valid for a year, along with a bundle of partner discounts.
eligibility: Company must be less than 2 years old
Must have raised under US$5 million
PostHog account created on or after 1 January 2023, using a company email domain
Companies owned by an ineligible parent group do not qualify; credits granted once per founder/organisation
benefits: US$50,000 in PostHog credits valid for 12 months
US$5,000 Depot credit, US$1,500 off an Incident.io team plan and 50% off Speakeasy for 6 months
PostHog merchandise
items.note: Rolling. You must first move to a usage-based paid plan, then submit the startup form from a company-email account; credits apply automatically on acceptance. From 14 Sept 2026 credits cannot be spent on PostHog's AI features (PostHog AI, Replay Vision, Inbox, etc.). Support is community/standard only. YC companies have a separate, non-stackable deal.

items.title: Mixpanel for Startups — First Year Free (Worth $145,000)
items.org: Mixpanel
items.summary: Mixpanel's Startup Plan gives eligible early-stage companies a year of its full analytics suite free, covering up to 1 billion events and 1 million session replays with all add-ons.
eligibility: Must meet Mixpanel's company-age and funding limits (confirmed on the application form)
Must never have been on a paid Mixpanel plan or used another Mixpanel offer
Must not have previously joined the startup program
Must start sending data to Mixpanel within 90 days of acceptance
benefits: All advanced reports, including Signal and Experiments with Feature Flags
Data Pipelines, Group Analytics, Warehouse Connectors and Session Replay
Up to 1 billion events and 1 million session replays in the year
items.note: Rolling; apply at mixpanel.com/startups-apply (choose a referral partner or 'no referral partner'). The plan does not support BAAs or MSAs. No second free year: afterwards move to Free, Growth or Enterprise. Accounts that don't send data within 90 days are removed.

items.title: 500 Global Flagship Accelerator (San Francisco) — Rolling Applications
items.org: 500 Global
items.amount: Up to $50K upfront, with up to $1M more possible
items.summary: 500 Global's four-month, in-person Flagship Accelerator in San Francisco invests up to $50,000 in accepted companies at entry, with follow-on of up to $1 million possible as they hit milestones; applications are reviewed for the next batch.
eligibility: Open from day zero through early users, revenue or pilots
Founders must be in the US or plan to be there within six months
Highly selective; aimed at exceptional founding teams
Acceptance does not guarantee investment
benefits: Up to US$50,000 initial investment
Potential follow-on of up to US$1 million
Four-month in-person programme in San Francisco with 500 Global's network
items.note: Rolling: the current batch runs 30 Nov 2026 – 9 Apr 2027, so new applications are considered for the following batch. Requires US relocation (Indian founders need suitable visas). Equity/SAFE terms are not published on the page; confirm before accepting.

items.title: Nexa Lighthouse — Climate & Health Innovation Call (Asia-Pacific), Deadline Extended
items.org: Grand Challenges Canada and AVPN, with funding partners including the Novo Nordisk Foundation, Bayer Foundation, India Health Fund, Sanofi Foundation and Temasek Foundation
items.summary: Grand Challenges Canada has pushed back the deadline for Nexa Lighthouse, its Transition-to-Scale call for proven innovations in Asia and the Pacific that help health systems cope with climate-driven risks: extreme heat, poor air quality and mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue and malaria.
eligibility: Organisations incorporated in, and implementing in, an eligible Asia-Pacific country (the country list is in Appendix B of the funding document; India Health Fund is a funding partner)
The innovation must already be proven and ready to expand. Untested ideas are not funded.
Must fit one of two themes: climate-informed early warning and monitoring (heat, air quality, changing mosquito ecology) or climate-responsive patient care for those conditions
Proposals are accepted only through GCC's Fluxx portal
benefits: Transition-to-Scale funding of roughly US$250,000 to US$2 million per innovation, sized to its maturity
Support and network access from Grand Challenges Canada, AVPN and corporate and philanthropic funders across Asia
A route to scale across several Asia-Pacific health systems
items.note: Reopened: the deadline is extended to 8 Dec 2026, 2:00 pm ET (12:30 am IST on 9 Dec). Submissions go through gcc.fluxx.io only. Before applying, read the funding document for the country list, the form of funding (grant or other instrument) and the Stage 1 questions.

items.title: UNICEF Venture Fund — Call for Open Source Frontier Tech Solutions
items.org: UNICEF Venture Fund (UNICEF Office of Innovation)
items.summary: UNICEF's Venture Fund is taking applications from early-stage for-profit startups building open-source frontier technology, such as AI/ML, blockchain, quantum or nanotech, that could improve children's lives. Selected startups receive up to US$100,000 in equity-free funding.
eligibility: Registered as a private for-profit company in a UNICEF programme country (India is one)
Must have a working prototype; at the idea stage you are not eligible
The solution must already be open source, or the company must commit to open-sourcing it
Application must be written in English; women-led and youth-led (under 35) teams are encouraged to apply
benefits: Up to US$100,000 in equity-free funding (UNICEF can pay in fiat or crypto)
Technical mentorship and portfolio support from the UNICEF Office of Innovation
Visibility and links to UNICEF country offices and partners
items.note: Closes 31 Jan 2027, 11:59 pm CET (4:29 am IST on 1 Feb). The link is UNICEF's official application form. UNICEF's general open-call web page still shows an older call as closed, so applicants should rely on the form. Any funded work has to be released under an open-source licence.

items.title: 18th Innovation World Cup (Industry, Industrial AI, Robotics, Security, Mobility)
items.org: Innovation World Cup Series (WT | Wearable Technologies AG), with partners including STMicroelectronics, EBV Elektronik, Siemens and Bosch
items.amount: In-kind prizes (no cash stated); pitch at HANNOVER MESSE 2027
items.summary: A free, long-running global contest for startups, scale-ups and SMEs in industrial tech. The top 15 in Industry, Industrial AI, Robotics, Mobility and Security pitch at HANNOVER MESSE 2027, and entrants are also considered for sponsor awards such as the ST Innovation Challenge and the EBV Innovation Hero.
eligibility: Open to startups, scale-ups and innovative SMEs from any country
The product must fit one of the categories: Industry, Industrial AI, Robotics, Security or Mobility (wearables and smart city/home solutions have separate finals)
There is no stated limit on company age or stage; a working solution makes for a stronger entry
Free to enter online
benefits: Finalist pitch slot at HANNOVER MESSE 2027 in front of corporates and investors
Free development kits from STMicroelectronics and Würth Elektronik, plus access to labs and testing facilities
Engineering and supply-chain support through the EBV Innovation Hero award (sensor, IoT, edge AI and robotics solutions)
Marketing package, global media coverage and a place in the Hall of Fame
items.note: Main deadline is 4 Feb 2027, 23:59 CET (4:29 am IST on 5 Feb). The separate EBV Innovation Hero page gives 11 Feb 2027, 11:59 pm CET, but describes that award as for EMEA startups. No cash prize is itemised. The headline 'worth US$500K+' is mostly in-kind, and the page does not say whether travel to Germany is covered.

items.title: WFP Innovation Challenge — Rolling Applications
items.org: UN World Food Programme (WFP) Innovation Accelerator, Munich
items.summary: The WFP Innovation Accelerator takes applications year-round from startups and organisations working on hunger, emergency response and resilient food systems. It reviews them whenever funding or a programme opens and can offer equity-free funding and pilots with WFP country operations.
eligibility: A registered legal entity, for-profit or non-profit
The innovation must be at least at MVP stage; proof of concept and early traction are preferred
Must already operate, or be willing to operate, in one of WFP's 120+ countries and territories (WFP runs a large India programme)
The proposal must explain how WFP fits the long-term strategy and include a plan for a sprint and a path to scale
Focus areas: emergency response, supply chain, smallholder farmers and food systems, school meals, resilience and livelihoods, nutrition
benefits: Equity-free funding to pilot and scale with WFP
Access to WFP operations and country offices for field implementation
Innovation consulting and mentoring, including from corporate partners
Visibility through WFP's channels
items.note: Rolling with no closing date. Applications are reviewed in batches when funding or a programme becomes available, so there may be long waits, and WFP says it cannot reply to every applicant. The page does not state a grant size. Separate, dated calls (such as Hiper for emergency-response products) are listed at innovation.wfp.org/apply.

items.title: UK Global Entrepreneur Programme (GEP) — Free Support to Set Up in the UK
items.org: Department for Business and Trade (DBT), UK Government
items.amount: Free dealmaker mentoring + Innovator Founder visa endorsement (no cash)
items.summary: A UK government programme in which experienced entrepreneur 'dealmakers' mentor high-growth, IP-led overseas companies that want to put their global HQ, a subsidiary or an R&D centre in the UK. It also helps founders get endorsed for the Innovator Founder visa.
eligibility: A company not yet based in the UK that plans a UK HQ, subsidiary or R&D centre
Usually £250K to £10M+ in revenue (depending on sector); earlier-stage firms should have raised over £500K and hold registered IP
Over 20% growth across three years (or meeting the OECD high-growth definition), plus strong investor backing
A founder or co-founder must relocate to the UK, or a senior strategic role must be created there
benefits: Free one-to-one strategic mentoring from a GEP dealmaker
Help towards the Innovator Founder visa endorsement (3 years' leave for the founder and eligible family)
Introductions to UK investors, research partners and commercial networks
Onboarding into the UK ecosystem; no fees and no equity taken
items.note: No fixed deadline: submit your details for an initial assessment.
